message.content: A cell that contains more than one nucleus is generally referred to as a **multinucleated cell**. In biology, such cells are often called a **syncytium** (plural: syncytia) when they arise from the fusion of several individual cells. A common example in medicine is the **multinucleated giant cell**, which can appear in granulomatous inflammation. If you’re thinking specifically about blood, the bone‑marrow precursor known as a **megakaryocyte** is a large cell that typically has many lobulated nuclei and gives rise to platelets.
